title: Requested Weekly Frequency on Work Conditioning and Work Hardening Extensions
content:
# Requested weekly frequency

On an extension of the Work Conditioning Program or the Work Hardening Program under a Workers' Compensation Referral, the weekly frequency requested from the adjuster depends on the worker's recent attendance — both in the Appointment Series funded by the referral and in the missed program days reported to the adjuster.

**Rule.** The requested weekly frequency is two (2) program days where two or more appointments in the funded appointment series with dates in the last month were no-shows and two or more missed program days with dates of service in the last month have been reported to the adjuster, three (3) program days where exactly one such appointment was a no-show and at least one such missed program day has been reported, and the program's maximum program days per week otherwise.

The program's maximum program days per week is 5 in both the Work Conditioning Program and the Work Hardening Program (the other programs list 2, 3, 3 and 2).

## What is counted

- **No-shows** — appointments in the Appointment Series whose funding is this referral, recorded as no-shows, with appointment dates in the last month.
- **Reported missed program days** — missed program days on the referral reported to the adjuster, with dates of service in the last month.

## Truth table

| No-shows in the funded Appointment Series, last month | Missed program days reported, last month | Requested weekly frequency |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | 2 or more | 2 program days |
| 2 or more | 1 | the program's maximum |
| 2 or more | 0 | the program's maximum |
| exactly 1 | 1 or more | 3 program days |
| exactly 1 | 0 | the program's maximum |
| 0 | any | the program's maximum |

## Case (hypothetical)

A Work Conditioning Program worker had two no-shows in the funded Appointment Series last month, and only one missed program day has been reported to the adjuster in the same period. Two no-shows but fewer than two reported missed days, and not exactly one no-show: the program's maximum program days per week are requested.
